sources.text: Faculty Profiles Back to Faculty Profiles Kolade Adebowale Assistant Professor, Bioengineering Shu Chien-Gene Lay Department of Bioengineering at the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering Cancer immunology; immune cell therapy; biomaterials; mechanotransduction Adebowale's lab seeks to integrate engineering design principles to cancer immunology to enable rational engineering and prediction of effective, next-generation immune cell therapies. Adebowale strives to understand how the complex functionality of the immune system arises from mechanical cues and simple biophysical principles. He is passionate about educating and training the next generation of engineers from all backgrounds and promoting a culture of inclusive excellence. Capsule Bio: Before joining the Jacobs School of Engineering in March, 2025, Adebowale was a postdoctoral fellow in bioengineering at Harvard University / Wyss Institute. He received a PhD in chemical engineering from Stanford University. Selected Publications: Google Scholar Publications Update your profile Email: kadebowale@ucsd.edu MIND Lab

sources.title: Research Centers and Institutes | Jacobs School of Engineering
sources.text: Research Centers and Institutes Impact through relevance The Jacobs School of Engineering is home to many research centers and institutes focused on tough technology challenges that no lab, discipline or industry can solve alone. These centers and institutes bring UC San Diego researchers from different disciplines together to collaborate with one another, and with industry, government and academic partners. This model encourages strategic partnerships – the kinds of collaborations that are critical for preparing future generations of engineers while also moving research innovations from research labs to the real world. The Jacobs School has launched 14 of these research centers and institutes since 2014. They complement a robust set of research centers launched prior to 2014. Contact the industry relations team to learn more.
